title: Hydra prober conformance playbook: dedicated throughput measurement, autoscaler behavior, and customer acceptance
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a repeatable, instrumented, and customer-facing throughput conformance suite for Dedicated capacity that validates: (1) sustained throughput under committed capacity, (2) tail latency and microburst headroom, and (3) autoscaler correctness and safety under realistic tenant mixes. This ticket defines 'Hydra Prober' — an end-to-end playbook, harness, and acceptance checklist to be used both by SRE/Onboarding and by Solutions during customer pilots.

Objectives:
- Define a canonical load harness that can run deterministic scenarios (sustained QPS, microburst, ramp/ramp-down, tenant-mix) and replay customer traces.
- Specify benchmarking methodology, telemetry queries, and pass/fail gating criteria for throughput guarantees and tail-latency SLOs.
- Produce a customer acceptance checklist and runbook that Solutions and SRE can execute during Dedicated onboarding and renewal labs.
- Integrate the harness with existing CI and the observability stack so evidence artifacts (graphs, CSVs, logs) are archivable and shareable.

Scope and non-goals:
In-scope: harness code, scenario definitions, telemetry dashboard templates, acceptance checklist, and a short ops runbook for triage.
Out-of-scope: wholesale changes to autoscaler internals or model runtime optimization; those will be separate follow-ups if tests surface regressions.

Benchmark methodology (high level):
1) Workload taxonomy: define 4 canonical profiles — Sustained Steady (S1), Microburst (M1), Tenant Mix (T1), Replay (R1). Each profile documents request size distribution, sequence length, KV cache hit assumptions, and percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
2) Deterministic staging: every run begins from a fresh cluster state, pins model/quantization version, and seeds any randomized client behavior.
3) Ramp and sustain windows: ramp-up no faster than 10% qps/sec until target, sustain for configurable window (default 30m), then ramp-down. Microburst includes short spikes at 2x-4x sustained for 30s-2m.
4) Telemetry collection: collect per-request latency histograms, per-worker GPU util, token/sec, queue lengths, and autoscaler events. Export traces and KV cache deltas.
5) Statistical verdicts: use quantile comparisons (p50/p90/p95/p99), sustained throughput delta vs contract, and resource-safety checks (no OOMs, no unbounded queue growth).

Acceptance gates (customer-facing):
- Throughput: observed sustained token/sec within ±7% of committed capacity over the sustain window.
- Tail latency: p99 <= contractual tail latency (configurable per customer) for 95% of the sustain window.
- Autoscaler: no oscillation events (>3 scale actions within 5m) and graceful scale-down (no request drops during cool-down).
- Safety: zero worker OOMs, <0.1% request errors, and successful fallback to idle model variant if a node fails.

Instrumentation and artifacts to produce:
- Grafana dashboard template: /d/redwood/hydra-prober (panels: throughput, p50/p90/p99, gpu-util, queue-length, scale-events).
- Exported CSV bundle per run: run-metadata.csv, per-request-latencies.csv, autoscaler-events.csv, host-metrics.csv.
- Canonical run manifest (JSON) listing model version, runtime flags, seed, tenant-mix, and commit SHAs.
- GitHub PR template for any test-rule changes and a Confluence page with step-by-step run instructions.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Synthetic vs replay: we will support both. Synthetic scenarios are deterministic and cheap; replay provides fidelity to customer traffic but may be noisy. Acceptance runs for contract should require a synthetic T1+R1 combo.
- Run duration: longer runs (30m) provide stability signals but take more CI resources. Default: 30m sustain, optional 2h long-run for large customers.
- Aggressiveness of autoscaler checks: conservative thresholds reduce false positives but delay detection of regressions. We err on stricter detection for onboard signoff and looser checks for nightly regression.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Checkout harness branch and deploy test cluster in dedicated-staging.
2) Upload run manifest and start run via hydra-cli: hydra run --manifest run.json --out artifacts/.
3) Monitor Grafana. If p99 breaches early, abort run and capture debug dump: hydra-cli dump --run-id <id>.
4) On failure, triage: check model version mismatch, KV-cache warming, and autoscaler logs. Escalate to runtime-eng if GPU errors/ooms.

Customer acceptance checklist (to be signed by Solutions + Customer engineer):
- Scenario(s) executed: list S1/T1/M1/R1 as applicable.
- Signed artifact bundle: CSVs, dashboard snapshots, and run manifest uploaded to the customer's onboarding folder.
- Acceptance verdict: Pass / Conditional Pass / Fail with reasoning (latency delta, throughput shortfalls, autoscale events).
- Recommended action: If conditional, specify remediation (e.g., increase committed capacity, tune batching, enable prefix cache).

Risks and mitigations:
- Non-determinism from multi-tenant noise: mitigate by tenant isolation or running during low-noise windows and repeating runs.
- False negatives from transient infra flakiness: require two consecutive failing runs before failing signoff.
- Customer expectations mismatch: ensure Solutions share run methodology and gating thresholds before tests.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Implement hydra-prober harness skeleton and scenario DSL (Samir).
- [ ] Grafana dashboard templating and CSV exporter (observability).
- [ ] Confluence runbook and customer checklist for Solutions.
- [ ] Pilot with two ongoing Dedicated customers in March to validate thresholds.

Expected deliverables:
- hydra-prober repo under infra/tests with three scenario definitions and CLI runner.
- Dashboards and exportable artifact bundle.
- Customer-facing acceptance PDF and onboarding checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Hydra CLI can execute S1/T1/M1/R1 scenarios and produce artifact bundle
Grafana dashboard template exists and links to run artifacts
Automated verdict logic produces Pass/Conditional/Fail and stores verdict in artifacts/summary.json
Runbook and customer-facing acceptance checklist published in Confluence
Two successful pilot runs with different tenant mixes and one documented conditional failure case
